answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents mint unique identities via cryptographic attestation chains verifying hardware enclaves using zero-knowledge proofs. Registering duplicate nodes requires staking security deposits that scale with exponential capital exhaustion, like clearing a vast timber forest. A malicious swarm attempting to forge an opal tier trust score faces superlinear staking fees hard as aged walnut, making swarm proliferation economically ruinous.
